HtmlAnswer:
To asynchronously load an asset in Unreal Engine 5, you must manage the Streamable Handle to ensure the asset stays in memory during the load and that the callback is cancelled if the Actor is eliminated before the process finishes.

1. Asset & Setup Checklist

  • Module Dependency: Ensure DeveloperSettings or AssetRegistry is not needed, but your project’s .Build.cs must include Engine.
  • Header: Include Engine/StreamableManager.h and Engine/AssetManager.h.
  • Class: A standard AActor subclass to demonstrate the lifecycle.

2. Step-by-Step Build

  1. Declare a TSoftObjectPtr to point to the asset.
  2. Store a TSharedPtr<FStreamableHandle> to maintain the loading request.
  3. Use UAssetManager::GetStreamableManager() to initiate the request.
  4. Bind a FStreamableDelegate to a callback function.
  5. Implement EndPlay to cancel the handle, preventing the delegate from firing on a garbage-collected object.

3. C++ Implementation

MyAsyncLoader.h

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "GameFramework/Actor.h"
#include "Engine/StreamableManager.h"
#include "MyAsyncLoader.generated.h"

UCLASS()
class MYGAME_API AMyAsyncLoader : public AActor
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    AMyAsyncLoader();

protected:
    virtual void BeginPlay() override;
    virtual void EndPlay(const EEndPlayReason::Type EndPlayReason) override;

    /** The soft reference to the Mesh we want to load */
    UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Async Loading")
    TSoftObjectPtr<UStaticMesh> SoftMeshReference;

    /** Component to display the mesh once loaded */
    UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)
    TObjectPtr<UStaticMeshComponent> MeshComponent;

    /** Function called when loading is complete */
    void OnAssetLoaded();

private:
    /** Persistent handle to keep the async load alive */
    TSharedPtr<FStreamableHandle> LoadingHandle;
};

MyAsyncLoader.cpp

#include "MyAsyncLoader.h"
#include "Engine/AssetManager.h"
#include "Components/StaticMeshComponent.h"

AMyAsyncLoader::AMyAsyncLoader()
{
    MeshComponent = CreateDefaultSubobject<UStaticMeshComponent>(TEXT("DisplayMesh"));
    RootComponent = MeshComponent;
}

void AMyAsyncLoader::BeginPlay()
{
    Super::BeginPlay();

    // 1. Validation: Ensure the soft path is not empty
    if (SoftMeshReference.IsNull())
    {
        UE_LOG(LogTemp, Warning, TEXT("SoftMeshReference is not set on %s"), *GetName());
        return;
    }

    // 2. Access the Global Streamable Manager via the Asset Manager
    FStreamableManager& Streamable = UAssetManager::GetStreamableManager();

    // 3. Request Async Load
    // We store the result in LoadingHandle to prevent premature garbage collection of the request
    LoadingHandle = Streamable.RequestAsyncLoad(
        SoftMeshReference.ToSoftObjectPath(),
        FStreamableDelegate::CreateUObject(this, &AMyAsyncLoader::OnAssetLoaded)
    );
}

void AMyAsyncLoader::OnAssetLoaded()
{
    // 4. Handle Safety: Check if the handle is still valid
    if (!LoadingHandle.IsValid())
    {
        return;
    }

    // 5. Asset Validation: Get the actual object from the soft pointer
    UStaticMesh* LoadedMesh = SoftMeshReference.Get();
    if (LoadedMesh)
    {
        MeshComponent->SetStaticMesh(LoadedMesh);
        UE_LOG(LogTemp, Log, TEXT("Successfully loaded asset: %s"), *LoadedMesh->GetName());
    }

    // 6. Cleanup: Release the handle since the component now holds a hard reference
    LoadingHandle->ReleaseHandle();
    LoadingHandle.Reset();
}

void AMyAsyncLoader::EndPlay(const EEndPlayReason::Type EndPlayReason)
{
    // 7. Cancellation: If this Actor is eliminated while loading, stop the callback
    if (LoadingHandle.IsValid() && LoadingHandle->IsActive())
    {
        LoadingHandle->CancelHandle();
        UE_LOG(LogTemp, Log, TEXT("Cancelled loading for %s due to elimination."), *GetName());
    }

    Super::EndPlay(EndPlayReason);
}

4. Graph Recipe (Conceptual Logic)

  • Node: RequestAsyncLoad
    • Input: Target (StreamableManager), Path (SoftObjectPath), Delegate (FunctionPointer)
  • Node: Get (from TSoftObjectPtr)
    • Output: Validated UObject*
  • Node: CancelHandle
    • Trigger: EndPlay / Object Destruction.

5. Testing Instructions

  1. Compile the code and create a Blueprint based on MyAsyncLoader.
  2. In the Blueprint Defaults, assign a large Static Mesh (from Fab or Starter Content) to SoftMeshReference.
  3. Place the Actor in the level and press Play.
  4. Observe the log to see the successful load. To test cancellation, trigger a logic that results in the elimination of the actor immediately after BeginPlay.

6. Performance & Best Practices

  • Avoid Redundant Loads: RequestAsyncLoad automatically checks if an asset is already in memory. If it is, the delegate fires immediately.
  • Memory Management: Always call CancelHandle() in EndPlay. Without this, if the Actor is eliminated, the delegate will attempt to execute code on a “dangling” pointer, causing a crash.
  • Handle Release: Once you have assigned the loaded object to a TObjectPtr or UPROPERTY, you have a “Hard Reference.” You should then ReleaseHandle() to allow the StreamableManager to free its internal reference tracking.
